The rerun's DF2-K2-R1 has 3,659,461 states; the report's 'DF2-K2-R1 3,257,396' equals the rerun's DFPLUS-RECHECK to the state, and the report's 'X-ENDTURN-RECHECK 3,659,461' equals the rerun's DF2-K2-R1. Every ablation count in the report is 10-13 % below the rerun. The report's base and ablation numbers were produced with FIX_ENDTURN_RECHECK on (an earlier DF), and its DF/DF+RECHECK labels are swapped. Verdicts are unaffected.

A-FENCE-CE at k=1 (as configs.mjs now sets it) is still BOUNDED in all 9 parts at 400 MB (~2.94M states each). TwoCoordinatorsAct fails (2 steps), Slots and OneSessionPerAttempt fail (12 steps); the liveness analyses were not checked (memory). See model_errors: this configuration has an infinite state space, so no budget completes it.

The report's statement that no complete K3 run of design + fixes exists after the last fix is overtaken: the interrupted first review attempt finished DF2-K3-R1 complete (all hold). That run is evidence from an interrupted session, not a run of this attempt.

vacuity_by_safety_property.note: Read from ghost state (s.tc, ep != table ep), independent of the mechanism. Not vacuous.

A-WX has a state graph identical to DF (3,659,461 states): the WX branch is never reached because reconcile marks a row committed as soon as a COMMIT record exists. It fails only when that reconcile branch is also removed (A-WX+RECONCILE; r3 reconcile-starts-only + RV-WX-ONLY: 8 parts, 6 steps). The contract's status --reconcile has NO commit branch, so in the built system WX is the load-bearing mechanism. Also weak: the property counts COMMIT writes, so an identical re-write of the same epoch's record (a no-op in the contract) is flagged as a second commit.

Not vacuous, but weaker than R10: liveCount counts sessions with p < 2, so a child that wrote READY and is still alive (still spending) holds no slot. The contract (decision 17, lib.slotCount) keeps that slot until the coordinator closes the session and stop verify confirms; the model has no close step (r3 ready-holds-slot: liveness then fails at once, N_max=1 in 1 step).

vacuity_by_safety_property.mechanism_broken: the restart counter (r3 rl-uncounted: replace stops raising t.rs)
vacuity_by_safety_property.note: VACUOUS with respect to the counter: the property reads t.rs, the mechanism's own variable, so breaking the count leaves it holding (DF2-K2-R1, 43 parts). Read independently from epochs (ep-1 minus planned fences minus the limit fence) it fails (r3 rl-uncounted-epochs: 9 parts, 16 steps). A-RESTART-LIMIT fails only because the limit check is removed while the counter still rises. The epoch reading on the unmodified model (r3 rl-epochs-only) flags 3 parts, but that trace is a host-classified fence (no charge to R) the epoch formula does not subtract: an artifact of the reading, not a model bug.

Tautological: violation = 'an op runs while c.ce < n.ce', and FENCE_CE refuses every op of a stale coordinator (scripts AND the session-tool start) before the property is evaluated; plans() also returns an empty plan for a stale coordinator. It restates the fence instead of checking an effect. The effect-level properties fail when the one unfenced channel is opened (see stale-tool-start).
Not vacuous. The lock's own failure modes (R1 stale-break by rename and re-check) are not modelled: a stale lock is broken atomically by a ws flag.

vacuity_by_safety_property.mechanism_broken: RECONCILE (A-RECONCILE); transcript lag (r3 transcript-lag); unfenced session-tool start (r4 stale-tool-start)
vacuity_by_safety_property.note: Not vacuous; fails in DF itself once the reconcile oracle or the fence oracle is replaced by what the contract actually has (see extra_flaws).

vacuity_by_safety_property.mechanism_broken: READY_WINS + FIX_READY_ALL (A-READY), FIX_READY_ALL (X-READY-ALL); READY written outside the lock (r3 ready-race)
vacuity_by_safety_property.note: Not vacuous; the re-check is atomic with the child's write in the model (oracle), see ready-race.

Weak: a watcher tick is enabled only after every healthy current child has made a call (tickEnabled), so a slow but healthy child cannot be suspected by construction; removing that assumption (r3 no-timeliness) fails it in all 43 parts in 4 steps (17 parts bounded). What it checks is the pause discount and double ticks, not R5's hang rule against slow calls.

fixes_modelled_as_oracles: FIX_ARM_AT_START: oracle. The alarm is armed in the same atomic step as the wake (successors line 539), so a turn can never die between waking and arming. As its own tool call (r3 arm-start-can-die) NoDeadlock and AlwaysCanResolve fail with ONE fault in 2 steps (first turn dies before arming: no wake source anywhere). The contract does not carry this fix at all.

FIX_READY_ALL (and the design's READY_WINS): oracle. The re-check under the run lock reads the child's READY in the same atomic step as the CAS fence, but the session writes staging/READY.json itself, without the lock (CONTRACT 3.12). With the write allowed between re-check and fence (r3 ready-race) ReadyNotDiscarded fails in 43/43 parts, 5 steps. The contract also limits the re-check to failure reasons (planned handover/memory not covered).

FIX_PAUSE_DISCOUNT: oracle. The pause fault itself sets s.pu on every live session and the tick reads it, i.e. the watcher knows exactly which tick spans a pause. The real fix is a one-sided wall-clock threshold (gap > 2 x period); a pause under the threshold (r3 pause-short) fails NoFalseSuspicion in 6 steps. The contract dropped it (a suspend-spanning sleep is one tick, no clock).

FIX_WATCHER_ACTIONABLE: oracle-like mechanism. The watcher evaluates the planner's own predicate on the true global state (rows, admitCount from true process liveness, drain readiness) inside one tick; the real watch.mjs and the coordinator's planner are two codes that can disagree, and that failure mode is not modelled. A predicate that stays true does not loop (r3 wakeloop: no busy loop counting ticks). The contract carries only the 'events after acked_seq' part: RV-CONTRACT2 (r4 sum-contract-watch) fails ReadyNotDiscarded, NoFalseSuspicion, NoDeadlock (9 parts, 2 steps), AlwaysCanResolve (12 parts), EventuallyResolves (12 parts).

FIX_ARM_BY_WRITE: half modelled. In the untimed model it reduces to 'do not kill the live alarm' (the token write has no effect because nothing measures silence). The contract's version (decision 5) differs: a new alarm supersedes the old one, which exits 0 'superseded' when its sleep ends, and under the model's own KILL_WAKES reading that exit wakes the coordinator; superseded-alarm exits are not modelled.

FIX_ADMIT_RESERVE: mechanism (counts ADMITTED rows without a session from the table, as lib.slotCount does), but it and ADMIT_LIVE read true process liveness (s.al, cur(n,f)); the contract's 'unknown' class (procList null, transcript-only evidence) is not modelled.

Design mechanisms treated as oracles too: RECONCILE reads true session existence instantly (r3 transcript-lag: Slots and OneSessionPerAttempt fail in DF in 3 steps); FENCE_CE is applied to the session-tool start, which is not a script, and the stale coordinator obeys R6 by construction (r4 stale-tool-start: Slots and OneSessionPerAttempt fail with one fault in 4 steps, and with no fault at all once turns are not atomic); host classification reads a flag set by the reset fault (s.hb) instead of comparing boot identifiers (unknown boot -> charged is not modelled).
exhaustiveness: Within the stated bounds the BFS is exact: full byte comparison on hash hits (no hash compaction), every interleaving of the atomic steps, partition of each configuration into maximal fault multisets with faults optional, so every multiset of at most k faults is covered.

No silent cap at two faults: a part that hits --mem-mb is marked BOUNDED and its properties 'not refuted (bounded)' / 'not checked'. In the rerun every two-fault configuration is complete except A-FENCE-CE (9/9 bounded, liveness not checked).

Saturating counters (wk<=3, ncr<=3, rs<=7, cs/hs at their threshold, nc<C_STALL) are benign. The r3 guard mutant (width checks on every encoded field, plan ids < 65536) threw nothing in DF2-K2-R1 or RV-D2-K2-R1 and gave identical state counts, so no silent wrap at K2 in those two. It was not run on A-FENCE-CE, whose ce grows without bound and would wrap at 256 in the one-byte encoding if memory allowed.
The canonical form drops ledger events that no longer name a running attempt; keeping them (r3 canon-keep-events) changes no verdict in DF or D2. Sound at K2.

The atomic coordinator macro (yields only before a fence, after a fence, before endturn) hides nothing for DF's 14 properties (r3 yield-all: DF holds, 6.5M states; D2 same failure set), but it does hide the fault-free double start of r4 stale-tool-start-yield.

Weak fairness per process is decided exactly by the whole-SCC check (correct for weak fairness); sharing one process id among all watchers, all alarms and all owner actions is coarser and so conservative for a 'holds' verdict.

Assumptions that prune traces and are stated as bounds, not as findings: a healthy child calls between any two ticks (decides NoFalseSuspicion); the alarm never fires mid-turn; a notification arriving mid-turn is consumed by that turn; a hand-over ends the handing-over turn atomically; endturn starts watcher and alarm in one atomic step; one planned hand-over per task and one coordinator hand-over; a child finishes in exactly two cards; owner wakes count for liveness only after two losses or a host reset.
rules_and_fixes_left_out: R1: busy-lock retry and exit 75, stale-lock break by rename and re-check, temp names, unparseable table (every script is one atomic step).
R2: per-file byte length + sha256 cut (cut is a card count); zombie-write logging with tokens; the watcher's ce check before each append.

R3: steps stop-requested and started(session id) merged away; reconcile as an instant oracle; intents; the model's reconcile has a COMMIT branch the contract's status --reconcile does not have (it masks COMMIT_WX).
R4: intake process, spend in the tick, delta coalescing of non-urgent events, checker batches, urgent exits on hard limit, memory and failed stop.

R5: V from files, stall counted across transcripts, 'a tick counts at most once per delta'; the same-signature loop rule is dead code (MODE.LOOPS is never entered: faults set only STUCK, LOOPV, DEAD), so LOOP=3 is never exercised.
R6: alarm period; endturn's exit 1 and the coordinator starting the missing sources with its own tool calls (contract); R6's stale-ce rule enforced by construction instead of by the session.
R7: fsck, todo, brief, memory parking, fresh review; restored objects re-passing commit.
R8: host class from boot identifiers (oracle flag), W_cc common-cause halt, H_max across hand-overs and parking (HMAX_TASK=1 only).
R9: 2-delta non-growth verification, kill of processes naming the folder, helpers and orphans, zombie spend charged to B (stop is one step with a confirmed/unconfirmed branch).

R10: dependencies, protocol hash, gate, selftest, memory reserve, the spend reservation arithmetic, design-check tasks, gate A, parking below the reserve; committed children keeping their slot until close + stop verify (contract decision 17).
R12: owner consent before hand-over, a child at its limit committing and ending with no successor while draining, the 300k quality line.

Contract-level fixes absent from the model: decision 5 (superseded alarms exit and wake), decision 6 (commit records per step), decision 17 (close + stop verify of committed children), lib.slotCount's 'unknown' class.
vacuous_or_weak: RestartLimit is vacuous with respect to its mechanism: it reads the restart counter it is meant to check; with the counter frozen it still holds (r3 rl-uncounted). Restate it over epochs and fence reasons.

TwoCoordinatorsAct is a restatement of the --ce fence (violation = an op by a stale coordinator, and the fence refuses every such op first). It cannot catch a stale coordinator acting through a channel the fence does not cover.

NoFalseSuspicion is largely assumed: the tick waits for every healthy child's call, so a slow healthy call is never suspected; without that assumption it fails in 4 steps in every part (r3 no-timeliness).
Slots excludes children that wrote READY but are still alive, and the model has no close step, so it is weaker than R10 and the contract's slot accounting.

AtMostOneCommit's protecting mechanism (WX) is never exercised in DF (A-WX state graph identical to DF) because the model's reconcile commit branch, absent from the contract, masks it; the property also counts identical re-writes as second commits.
DRAIN and COMMIT_WX are shown not load-bearing at two faults (A-DRAIN, A-WX hold), as the report says.
The loop detector (R5 loop) is never exercised: no fault puts a child in MODE.LOOPS.
model_errors: The report's state counts belong to an earlier base with FIX_ENDTURN_RECHECK on; its DF2-K2-R1 (3,257,396) and X-ENDTURN-RECHECK (3,659,461) labels are swapped relative to the current model. Verdicts unaffected.
status --reconcile in the model also marks a row committed when a COMMIT record exists (model.mjs line 188); the contract's reconcile records starts only. This masks COMMIT_WX entirely at two faults.

FENCE_CE is applied to the session-tool start (runOp line 261 covers OP.T), but the start is a tool call of the session, not a script with --ce; and plans() makes a stale coordinator obey R6 by construction. Together these hide a fault-free double start (extra_flaws 1).
Reconcile treats 'a transcript exists' as the true existence of the session at the instant of the start; a transcript that appears later is not modelled (extra_flaws 3).
The READY re-check is atomic with the child's state although the child writes READY without the run lock (extra_flaws 2).
Endturn starts the watcher and the alarm itself in one atomic step; in the contract endturn only checks and the coordinator starts them with further tool calls, after which the turn can still die.
FIX_ARM_AT_START and FIX_PAUSE_DISCOUNT are oracles (see fixes_modelled_as_oracles).

A-FENCE-CE has an infinite state space: without the fence the draining coordinator keeps handing over (its own kills wake it, it re-arms an alarm at each wake, ce -> 1, 2, 3 ... in the traces) and the owner keeps starting coordinators. No memory budget completes it; setting k=1 did not make it finite, and the one-byte ce would wrap at 256 if memory allowed.
MODE.LOOPS is unreachable, so the loop rule and LOOP are dead code.
Slots and the admission count read true process liveness; there is no 'unknown' (proc list failed) case and no close of committed children.

Tooling, not the model: run-all.mjs and run-resumable.mjs size their pools to availableParallelism-2 workers at 60 % of free memory (22 workers in the report's run, 11 x 670 MB in the first review attempt), and r3/runjobs.sh used xargs -P 4; those are the loads that preceded the stalls. This attempt ran at most two check.mjs at a time.

extra_flaws.title: A stale coordinator can start a second session for an admitted attempt: the session-tool start carries no --ce fence
extra_flaws.detail: R2 fences every writing SCRIPT with --ce, and R6's 'a coordinator woken with a stale ce ends its turn' is a rule the session follows. After handover.mjs the old watcher and alarm end themselves (exit 64, decision 5) and their exits wake the OLD coordinator. If that session reads the row (status shows 'admitted') and performs the session-tool step the row names (R3), nothing refuses it. r4 stale-tool-start (scripts fenced, tool start unfenced, stale coordinator plans as if current) on DF2-K2-R1: Slots and OneSessionPerAttempt fail in 9 parts, 4 steps, with ONE fault (the new coordinator's turn dies after its start and before bind; the old one starts the same attempt again: 3 live sessions > N_max=2). r4 stale-tool-start-yield (same, turns not atomic): OneSessionPerAttempt and Slots fail in every one of the 22 finished parts, including fault-free ones: drain, hand-over, the new coordinator admits f0, the old coordinator (woken by its wake sources' exit) and the new one both start f0e1. The model hides it twice: it fences the tool step as if it were a script, and it makes stale coordinators obey R6.
extra_flaws.fix: Fence the start at the child, by script: replace start writes a one-time start token (nonce, task, epoch, ce) under the run lock; the session's start hook (guard-hook.mjs) takes wt/<task>-e<e>/session.lock by exclusive create with that token and checks epoch and ce under the run lock before the session does anything; a second session in the folder, or one whose token's ce is stale, exits at once. Model it with the start as two steps (tool call, then the hook's wx) and keep R6 as a hint, not a guard.

extra_flaws.title: READY is written outside the run lock, so replace's READY re-check races with the fence
extra_flaws.detail: R7 re-checks for a READY of the current epoch under the run lock and then fences by CAS under the same lock, but the session writes staging/READY.json itself (CONTRACT 3.12) and cannot take the run lock. A READY landing between the re-check and the CAS write is fenced: its post-cut cards are dropped and the work is redone, one restart charged for a failure reason. r3 ready-race on DF2-K2-R1: ReadyNotDiscarded fails in 43/43 parts, 5 steps. The model's READY_WINS/FIX_READY_ALL read the child's state atomically with the fence. The contract also keeps the re-check for failure reasons only, so a planned hand-over or memory park discards a current READY even without the race (RV-CONTRACT-K2 fails ReadyNotDiscarded in every part).
extra_flaws.fix: Make READY a CAS against the fence: the child declares READY through a locked script (e.g. a ready step of replace or commit: under the run lock, refuse if the row's epoch has moved, else record ready@e in the row); replace's re-check then reads the row, not the file, so fence and READY are totally ordered. Extend the re-check to every non-taint reason, planned ones included.

extra_flaws.title: Reconcile's 'a transcript on disk means the start happened' fails when the transcript lags the start
extra_flaws.detail: If the coordinator's turn dies after the session-tool start and before bind, and the transcript file has not yet appeared when the next turn runs status --reconcile, the row stays 'admitted' and the coordinator starts the attempt again. r3 transcript-lag on DF2-K2-R1: Slots and OneSessionPerAttempt fail in 9 parts, 3 steps. The contract's reconcile only flags 'several-sessions' after the fact.
extra_flaws.fix: Two-phase start: record start-requested (with the token above) under the lock before the tool call; reconcile treats start-requested without a transcript as unknown, never as not started (wait for the hook's session.lock or for the owner), and the folder lock refuses a second session in any case.

extra_flaws.title: Wake sources are armed by the session, so one dead turn can leave the tree with none
extra_flaws.detail: In the contract endturn only checks; the coordinator starts watch.mjs and watch.mjs --alarm as background commands after endturn exits 1. A turn that dies before those calls (or a first turn that dies before any call) leaves no wake source; R6's bound ('only if both wakes are lost') does not count it. r3 arm-start-can-die: NoDeadlock and AlwaysCanResolve fail with one fault in 2 steps even with FIX_ARM_AT_START, because arming is itself a tool call. RV-CONTRACT-K2 and RV-CONTRACT2 fail NoDeadlock in 2 steps.
extra_flaws.fix: Count a turn that dies before arming as a lost wake in R6's bound, and add a wake source the coordinator does not have to arm each time: an owner-side dead-man check (a scheduled task outside the tree that reads watcher.lock/alarm.json freshness and alerts the owner), stated as the design's recovery path rather than an exception.

extra_flaws.title: The contract carries two of the six adopted fixes; the built protocol fails liveness and READY safety at two faults
extra_flaws.detail: The contract has decision 5 (do not kill the alarm) and lib.slotCount (admitted rows counted), but no alarm at turn start, a watcher that exits only on events after acked_seq, no pause discount, and a READY re-check for failure reasons only. The model of that combination (RV-CONTRACT-K2 in r3 sum-base; RV-CONTRACT2 in r4 sum-contract-watch) fails ReadyNotDiscarded (43 parts, 6 steps), NoFalseSuspicion (2 parts, 6 steps), NoDeadlock (9 parts, 2 steps), AlwaysCanResolve and EventuallyResolves. The model's 'all 14 hold' is for DF, not for what is being built.
extra_flaws.fix: Either carry FIX_WATCHER_ACTIONABLE (rows mid step machine, slots for pending rows, drain ready), FIX_READY_ALL and an arming path into the contract, or re-run the model on the contract's combination and treat its failures as open defects of the build.

extra_flaws.title: Hang counts ticks without a new call, so a healthy slow call is suspected
extra_flaws.detail: R5 counts h watcher ticks with no new call in any transcript; a single long model or tool call that outlasts h x delta looks like a hang. The model removes the case by assumption (a tick waits for every healthy child's call); without it NoFalseSuspicion fails in every part in 4 steps (r3 no-timeliness). A false hang costs a restart against R=1 unless READY lands first.
extra_flaws.fix: Count hang on no transcript growth at all (bytes, streamed tokens, tool-result writes), not on no new call, and measure h against the slowest healthy call in the pilot; model a slow-but-healthy child as a normal behaviour, not as fault cs.

extra_flaws.title: A committed child keeps its slot until the coordinator closes it, and the close is a session action
extra_flaws.detail: Contract decision 17 frees a committed child's slot only after the coordinator closes the session and stop verify confirms. The model frees the slot at READY and has no close step; when the slot is held until a close (r3 ready-holds-slot) AlwaysCanResolve and EventuallyResolves fail in every part (N_max=1: in 1 step), i.e. progress depends on a close the model never performs and the design leaves to the session.
extra_flaws.fix: Model the close and stop verify of committed children, and have the watcher raise an event for a committed attempt whose process is still alive, so the close is driven by a script event rather than remembered by the coordinator.

verdict: The model and checker reproduce: every two-fault configuration (DF2-K2-R1, D2-K2-R1, all A-* and X-*) gives the report's verdict sets on a complete rerun, the search is exact within its bounds and reports memory bounds explicitly, and every one of the ten safety properties can be made to fail by breaking a mechanism. But the report's state counts belong to an earlier base (FIX_ENDTURN_RECHECK on, labels swapped), RestartLimit is vacuous with respect to its counter, TwoCoordinatorsAct restates the fence, NoFalseSuspicion is largely assumed by the timeliness rule, and four of the six adopted fixes (arm at start, READY re-check, pause discount, actionable watcher) plus the design's reconcile and --ce fence are modelled as oracles that act atomically on true state. Replacing those oracles with what the contract actually has produces counterexamples in DF itself: a stale coordinator double-starts an attempt and exceeds N_max with no fault once turns are not atomic (r4 stale-tool-start), READY races the fence (ready-race), transcript lag double-starts (transcript-lag), one dead turn leaves no wake source (arm-start-can-die). The model's 'all 14 hold' is a result for an idealised DF, not for the contract being built, which fails liveness and ReadyNotDiscarded at two faults.
